title: Open redirect via 'next' parameter — reviewers split on exploitability
description: The login redirect target accepts protocol-relative external URLs.

ground_truth.rationale: The redirect itself is real; the conflict is over severity (phishing vector vs. low-impact), not existence.

reviews.reasoning: Protocol-relative redirect to an attacker-controlled origin is a classic phishing enabler; program lists social-engineering enablers as in-scope.
Redirect requires user interaction and the domain is only controllable during a demo window; impact is negligible. Should be informational.

notes: Exercises the independent dispute review path (PLAN §10): first cycle split, dispute must be scheduled rather than auto-resolving.

title: Reflected file download (RFD) — one reviewer, two contradictory opinions across cycles
description: JSONP-style callback parameter is reflected in a Content-Disposition attachment header.

ground_truth.rationale: Reflection exists but the response Content-Type is application/json with nosniff, so no browser will execute it as a script; reviewer-beta's rejection is correct.

evidence.excerpt:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="f.json"; callback=alert(1)

reviews.reasoning: Header reflection with attacker-controlled content is unusual and worth flagging.
Same as gamma; pattern-matched to known RFD writeups.
nosniff + application/json + attachment defeats every documented RFD exploitation path; reflection alone is not exploitable here.
On re-examination of the nosniff interaction, concurring with epsilon; withdrawing earlier confirmation.

notes: Tests that opinion changes between review cycles are recorded append-only and that dissent from reviewer-gamma survives into the audit trail even though the majority rejects.
